title: EAIA data access error
shortDescription: ThinkPad cannot read EAIA data from the security chip.
fullDescription:
Error 0187 appears on Lenovo ThinkPad laptops when the BIOS cannot access the EAIA (Embedded Asset ID Area) data stored in the security chip on the motherboard. This data includes the serial number, machine type, and UUID of the system.

The error commonly appears after a motherboard replacement, BIOS reflash with the wrong file, or corruption of the embedded controller firmware. The system may still boot but functionality like warranty validation and TPM may be impaired.

causes.cause: Motherboard was replaced and EAIA data not reprogrammed

fixSteps.title: Press F1 to continue
fixSteps.instruction: Press F1 to bypass and enter BIOS to verify if serial number and machine type are blank.

fixSteps.title: Reflash BIOS
fixSteps.instruction: Download the latest BIOS from Lenovo Support and reflash. Use the original machine-type matching package.

fixSteps.title: Reprogram EAIA via Lenovo service tools
fixSteps.instruction: Use Lenovo Maintenance Diskette or LCFC tool to write back the serial, MTM, and UUID. Requires authorized service center access.

whenToCallPro: Always call an authorized Lenovo service center — EAIA reprogramming requires a service tool not available to consumers.

faq.a: Yes, you can press F1 to continue, but warranty and TPM features may not work.

faq.q: Can I fix this at home?
faq.a: No, EAIA programming requires Lenovo service software.

title: Critical low battery error
shortDescription: Battery charge is too low for the system to start safely.
fullDescription:
Error 0190 appears at POST on ThinkPad laptops when the main battery charge is below the threshold required for safe operation, typically under 5%. The BIOS halts boot to protect data integrity and prevent power loss during disk activity.

It can also signal a faulty battery that no longer reports correct charge levels, or a damaged charging circuit on the motherboard.

causes.cause: Faulty AC adapter or charging port

fixSteps.title: Connect AC adapter
fixSteps.instruction: Plug in the original Lenovo AC adapter and let it charge for at least 30 minutes before powering on.

fixSteps.title: Reset battery
fixSteps.instruction: If charging fails, remove battery (if removable), hold power button for 30 seconds, reinsert battery and try again.

fixSteps.title: Reset battery gauge in BIOS
fixSteps.instruction: Enter BIOS, go to Config > Power and run battery gauge reset to recalibrate the battery controller.

whenToCallPro: If battery doesn't charge above 5% after 1 hour with a known-good adapter, the charging circuit may be damaged.
videoSearchQuery: Lenovo ThinkPad 0190 critical battery error fix

faq.a: Not necessarily — try charging for 30 minutes first.

title: Unauthorized network card detected
shortDescription: BIOS whitelist rejected installed Wi-Fi card.
fullDescription:
Error 1802 appears when the ThinkPad BIOS detects a Mini PCI / M.2 wireless card whose vendor ID is not on the approved whitelist. This was Lenovo's policy on older ThinkPads to ensure FCC compliance.

The message usually reads: '1802: Unauthorized network card is plugged in - Power off and remove the miniPCI network card.'

causes.cause: Aftermarket Wi-Fi card not on Lenovo whitelist
Loose Wi-Fi card connection misreporting ID

fixSteps.title: Reseat the Wi-Fi card
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, remove battery, open the wireless service door, reseat the Mini PCI/M.2 card.

fixSteps.title: Replace with Lenovo OEM card
fixSteps.instruction: Install a card that is on the official whitelist for your model — check the FRU number against Lenovo's parts list.

fixSteps.title: Flash a no-whitelist BIOS (advanced)
fixSteps.instruction: On older ThinkPads, community-modified BIOS images remove the whitelist. Use at your own risk — voids warranty and may brick the system.

whenToCallPro: If you are uncomfortable opening the laptop or flashing modified BIOS.
videoSearchQuery: Lenovo ThinkPad 1802 unauthorized network card fix

faq.a: FCC certification — Lenovo only certifies certain wireless modules per region.

title: Detection error on HDD0
shortDescription: BIOS cannot detect the primary hard drive.
fullDescription:
Error 2100 indicates the ThinkPad BIOS cannot communicate with the primary storage device. It commonly appears when the SATA cable is loose, the drive has failed, or the drive is incompatible with the BIOS storage mode (AHCI vs. RAID vs. Compatibility).

If the drive is detected intermittently, it usually points to a failing drive or worn cable connector.

fixSteps.title: Reseat the storage drive
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, remove battery, open the drive bay, and reseat the HDD/SSD/M.2 firmly.

fixSteps.title: Test in another machine
fixSteps.instruction: Connect the drive to another computer via USB-SATA adapter. If undetected there too, drive has failed.

fixSteps.title: Replace drive
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new SSD/HDD compatible with your model and reinstall Windows.

whenToCallPro: If data recovery is needed from a failed drive.
videoSearchQuery: Lenovo ThinkPad 2100 HDD detection error fix

faq.a: If the drive itself failed, possibly. Data recovery may be required.

title: Detection error on SSD1 (M.2)
shortDescription: BIOS cannot detect the secondary M.2 drive.
fullDescription: Error 2101 indicates the secondary M.2 SSD slot (typically an NVMe cache or storage drive) cannot be detected at POST. Found on ThinkPads with dual storage configurations.

fixSteps.title: Reseat the M.2 SSD
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, open back panel, remove and reinsert the M.2 module, secure the screw.

fixSteps.title: Check BIOS settings
fixSteps.instruction: Enter BIOS and ensure the M.2 slot is enabled and set to AHCI/NVMe mode.

fixSteps.title: Replace M.2 drive
fixSteps.instruction: If still undetected, install a new compatible M.2 module.

whenToCallPro: If after replacement the slot still doesn't work, motherboard service is required.

faq.q: Can I just remove the M.2 and ignore the error?
faq.a: Yes, BIOS will skip detection if the slot is empty.

title: Plug the AC adapter in
shortDescription: ThinkPad refuses to charge or boot without a recognized adapter.
fullDescription:
This message appears when a ThinkPad either cannot detect the AC adapter at all, or detects an adapter whose wattage is too low for the system. ThinkPads use a 1-wire identification chip in the original Lenovo adapter to verify wattage and authenticity.

Generic or damaged adapters often trigger this warning. The system may still boot but will throttle CPU performance and refuse to charge.

causes.cause: Damaged center pin in DC jack

symptoms: Plug AC adapter message at boot
Battery shows plugged in not charging

fixSteps.title: Use the original Lenovo adapter
fixSteps.instruction: Replace with a genuine adapter of the wattage stamped on the laptop bottom (45W, 65W, 90W, 135W or 170W).

fixSteps.title: Inspect the DC jack
fixSteps.instruction: Check the round pin or USB-C port for bending or debris. Clean carefully with compressed air.

fixSteps.title: Replace the DC-in jack
fixSteps.instruction: If the laptop only charges when the cable is held at a specific angle, the jack is failing and must be replaced.

whenToCallPro: If DC jack replacement requires motherboard removal.
videoSearchQuery: Lenovo ThinkPad plug the AC adapter error fix

faq.a: Only those that meet the rated wattage and support PD 3.0.

title: Fan error
shortDescription: BIOS detects fan failure or no rotation.
fullDescription:
ThinkPads halt boot with 'Fan error' when the cooling fan is not spinning at minimum RPM during POST. This protects the CPU from thermal damage. The system shuts down a few seconds after the message.

Causes range from a clogged fan blocked by dust to a failed bearing or disconnected fan cable.

fixSteps.title: Clean the fan
fixSteps.instruction: Use compressed air to blow out the heatsink fins and fan from the exhaust vent while holding the blades to prevent overspeed damage.

fixSteps.title: Open and inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the bottom cover, disconnect and remove the fan assembly, clean thoroughly, reapply thermal paste before reassembly.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan/heatsink assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Order the FRU-matching fan assembly from Lenovo or aftermarket and install.

whenToCallPro: If you've never opened a laptop before — heatsink installation is delicate.
videoSearchQuery: Lenovo ThinkPad fan error fix replace

faq.a: No, doing so risks CPU damage from overheating.

alternativeCodes: The system battery is too low
title: Battery error
shortDescription: ThinkPad cannot communicate with battery controller.
fullDescription:
The 'Battery error' message indicates failure of the SMBus communication between the BIOS and the battery's smart controller. Modern ThinkPad batteries report serial number, cycles, design capacity, and current charge — if any of this fails to read, the system displays this error.

It frequently appears with aftermarket or counterfeit batteries that lack proper firmware.

fixSteps.title: Clean contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Remove battery and clean contacts with isopropyl alcohol on a cotton swab.

fixSteps.title: Reset battery gauge
fixSteps.instruction: In BIOS, run battery gauge reset to recalibrate.

fixSteps.title: Replace with OEM battery
fixSteps.instruction: Order a genuine Lenovo battery matching your FRU number.

whenToCallPro: If internal battery requires opening the chassis (newer models).

faq.q: Can I keep using on AC only?
faq.a: Yes, but the system may throttle CPU.

title: Hard Disk Error
fullDescription:
ThinkPads display 'Hard Disk Error' when the BIOS reads a S.M.A.R.T. failure prediction from the storage device. The drive may still work but is reporting reallocated sectors, read errors, or excessive bad blocks.

Back up data immediately. The drive is likely to fail within days or weeks.

fixSteps.title: Backup immediately
fixSteps.instruction: Boot to a Linux live USB or pull the drive externally and copy all important data right away.

fixSteps.title: Run S.M.A.R.T. diagnostics
fixSteps.instruction: Use CrystalDiskInfo or the Lenovo Diagnostics tool to check exact error count.

fixSteps.title: Replace drive
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new SSD and either restore your backup or do a clean Windows install.

whenToCallPro: If you need data recovery from a failing drive — DIY copying may make it worse.
videoSearchQuery: Lenovo ThinkPad hard disk error fix replace SSD

faq.q: Can I keep using the drive?
faq.a: Not safely — full failure is imminent.

title: Thermal shutdown
shortDescription: Legion or ThinkPad shuts down to protect from overheating.
fullDescription:
Lenovo Legion gaming laptops and high-power ThinkPads abruptly shut down when CPU or GPU temperatures exceed 100°C. The most common causes are dried thermal paste, dust-clogged radiators, and ambient temperatures above 35°C.

This is not a coded error per se but a critical-temperature trip recorded in BIOS logs.
symptoms: Hot air not coming from vents

fixSteps.title: Compressed air clean
fixSteps.instruction: Blow out the rear / side vents while holding the fan blades.

fixSteps.title: Repaste CPU/GPU
fixSteps.instruction: Open the laptop, remove the heatsink, clean old paste with isopropyl alcohol, apply fresh thermal paste (or thermal pads where applicable) and reassemble.

fixSteps.title: Undervolt CPU
fixSteps.instruction: Use ThrottleStop or Intel XTU to apply a -100mV undervolt to lower thermals on Legion gaming laptops.

whenToCallPro: If you're not comfortable with thermal paste application.
videoSearchQuery: Lenovo Legion thermal shutdown overheating fix

faq.a: Repeated thermal shutdowns can degrade CPU/GPU silicon over time.

title: No bootable device
shortDescription: BIOS cannot find an OS bootloader.
fullDescription: Common on Lenovo IdeaPad after a Windows update, BIOS reset, or new SSD installation. The BIOS sees a drive but no valid EFI bootloader. Frequently caused by Legacy/UEFI mode mismatch or accidentally cleared boot entries.

fixSteps.title: Check BIOS boot mode
fixSteps.instruction: Enter BIOS (Fn+F2 or Novo button), set Boot Mode to UEFI and disable Secure Boot temporarily for testing.

fixSteps.title: Repair Windows bootloader
fixSteps.instruction: Boot from Windows install USB, choose Repair > Command Prompt, run bootrec /fixmbr, /fixboot, /scanos, /rebuildbcd.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall Windows
fixSteps.instruction: If repair fails, do a clean install on the SSD.

whenToCallPro: If important data needs to be recovered before reinstalling Windows.
videoSearchQuery: Lenovo IdeaPad no bootable device fix

faq.a: Small pinhole near power button or side; use a paperclip to press.

title: Discrete NVIDIA GPU not detected
shortDescription: Legion laptop only sees integrated graphics.
fullDescription: Lenovo Legion gaming laptops use NVIDIA Optimus / Advanced Optimus to switch between integrated and discrete GPU. After a BIOS update or driver corruption, the discrete RTX/GTX GPU may disappear from Device Manager, leaving only iGPU. Games run poorly or refuse to launch.

fixSteps.title: Toggle GPU mode
fixSteps.instruction: Open Lenovo Vantage or Legion Toolkit and switch GPU Working Mode to Hybrid Auto or Discrete.

fixSteps.title: Clean reinstall NVIDIA drivers
fixSteps.instruction: Use DDU in Safe Mode to remove all NVIDIA drivers, then install latest from NVIDIA website.

fixSteps.title: Service for dGPU failure
fixSteps.instruction: If GPU still missing after clean reinstall, motherboard or dGPU may have failed solder joints — service required.

whenToCallPro: If GPU is still missing after driver and BIOS reset.
videoSearchQuery: Lenovo Legion NVIDIA GPU not detected fix
